first_impression.reaction: Jumped to the FAQ first like I always do. The answers are straight times with a caveat, no fluff, so I went back up. The intro gives me the answer in the first paragraph and tells me the one variable that matters (sunset at the venue). No 'magical day' waffle. I'll keep reading.

journey.quote: The one time that fixes everything else is sunset at your venue on your date, so look that up first and build the photos, the lighting and the reception entrance around it.
journey.reaction: Good. A concrete rule I can actually act on instead of a mood board.

journey.section: The 4pm wedding timeline at a glance
journey.quote: Every clock time on this page is a planning example to adapt, not a rule.
journey.reaction: Honest about what this is. I'd rather be told it's an example than pretend it's gospel.

journey.section: How sunset shapes a 4pm wedding day
journey.quote: [Geoscience Australia's sunrise, sunset and twilight calculator](https://geodesyapps.ga.gov.au/sunrise) works these times out from the National Gazetteer of Australia.
journey.reaction: An actual government source I can check myself. That's the kind of thing that makes me trust the rest of the page.

journey.section: How sunset shapes a 4pm wedding day
journey.quote: The published time assumes a flat horizon.
journey.reaction: Nice catch on the limitation. Most sites wouldn't mention it. Telling me to walk the site at the same hour is practical.

journey.quote: By the end of evening civil twilight, when the centre of the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon, large objects can be seen but no detail can be made out without artificial light.
journey.reaction: Defined, sourced, and turned into a decision (lights on before this). Exactly what I want.

journey.section: Planning a 4pm ceremony at a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, works in your time zone, and is your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Here's the pitch. 'Plans payments' immediately makes me ask: do you take a cut from the venue or suppliers? Nothing here about how you're paid. The fee-in-writing line only shows up at the very bottom.

journey.quote: If you would rather hand the venue questions to one person, [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-timeline-4pm-ceremony&utm_content=secondary) pairs you with a Wedded Advisor for the whole plan.
journey.reaction: Second sales line in a few paragraphs, says nothing new. Feels like it's nudging me rather than informing me.

journey.quote: It suits couples who want a relaxed morning, softer light and a reception that runs into the evening.
journey.reaction: 'Softer light' than what? Earlier the page itself says 4pm is 'not yet golden hour' in summer. Needs a comparison or it reads like a vague claim.

journey.quote: In these examples, about an hour and a half, filled with photos and drinks, and longer without a first look.
journey.reaction: Checked it against the two run sheets: 4.30pm to 6pm, and 4.30pm to 6.30pm without. Numbers line up. Good.

journey.section: Plan the day around your light
journey.quote: If you would like to work it through with someone, a Wedded Advisor agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: This is the most useful sales sentence on the page for me. Fee in writing up front is a real trust signal. It still doesn't say how the fee works or whether suppliers pay you anything, but it's the right direction.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor paid: flat fee, percentage, or commissions from venues and suppliers?
Do you take a cut or mark-up on venue or vendor prices?
What does the fee actually include, in concrete terms, and what costs extra?
Is there a real wedding with a 4pm ceremony and its actual run sheet I can look at?
Where can I read independent reviews of Wedded Concierge?

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather hand the venue questions to one person, [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-timeline-4pm-ceremony&utm_content=secondary) pairs you with a Wedded Advisor for the whole plan.
turn_offs_found.why: Three Concierge pitches on one how-to page. The second one adds nothing and makes me wonder what the page is really for.

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, works in your time zone, and is your single point of contact from start to finish.
turn_offs_found.why: Service claim with no fee model attached. 'Payments' without saying how you get paid is exactly where I look for the catch.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the sunset and twilight section and the template table

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to work it through with someone, a Wedded Advisor agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: The closing CTA is the only one that gives me a reason to trust you (fee in writing first). I'd click through to look for the fee model and whether you take supplier commissions. I wouldn't fill in a form until that page answers it.
